applicableAreas: Buildings and facilities proximate to overhead electric lines
findings.comment: Overhead electric lines (OHE) are shown on plans but are not labeled with voltage classification. The 15-foot radial clearance requirement applies only to distribution facilities operating below 60kV (typically 12.47kV or 34.5kV in Austin). Without voltage labeling, the applicability of this distribution-specific requirement cannot be determined. Verify whether shown OHE lines are distribution or transmission facilities and label with operating voltage on utility plans.

agentTrace.observation: Vision review of Sheet 9 and 21 found OHE lines marked as '----OHE----' without any voltage notation (such as 12.47kV, 34.5kV, 69kV, etc.). Transmission notes on Sheet 3, Block 9 indicate transmission facilities exist, but specific voltage classification for the OHE shown is not provided.
agentTrace.reasoning: The code requirement for 15-foot radial clearance is specific to distribution primary and neutral conductors. If the shown OHE lines are transmission lines (≥60kV), different clearance and construction standards apply. The absence of voltage labeling creates ambiguity about which code requirements govern the clearance verification.

applicableAreas: Building roofs, overhangs, awnings, balconies, and canopies on Buildings 1-8 proximate to overhead electric conductors

The reference on Sheet 21 to 'See Sht. 19 for Profile' was investigated and found to be a water/wastewater utility sheet, not electrical profiles.

applicableAreas: All buildings, structures, and building projections within clearance distance of overhead electric facilities

findings.comment: Landscape plan (Sheet 31) shows fencing (identified by H.6 key notes for wooden privacy fences) but provides no clearance dimension callouts from the fence faces to outside conductor of overhead electric lines. applicableAreas: Fence post locations on site where existing utility poles are present

applicableAreas: Fencing shown in proximity to electric transmission lines if transmission easement applies

Without voltage confirmation and transmission easement delineation, cannot determine whether fences are beneath/within transmission easement and therefore subject to non-conductive material and grounding requirements. agentTrace.reasoning: Transmission fencing requirements apply only if fences are within or beneath transmission easement and only for transmission facilities (≥60kV). The plans acknowledge transmission facilities but do not clearly map transmission easement boundaries relative to proposed fences, making applicability determination not-verifiable.

applicableAreas: Retaining walls within clearance distance of overhead electric facilities

applicableAreas: Proposed driveways near overhead electric lines where vertical clearance applies
findings.comment: Grading plan (Sheet 11) and site plan (Sheet 9) show driveway alignments and elevations, but no cross-section views document vertical clearance from finished driveway surface to lowest point of overhead electric conductors (including telecommunications attachments). The 16-foot minimum clearance (parking without truck traffic) or 18-foot clearance (areas with truck traffic) must be verified through section views with dimension callouts. Provide section views showing driveway finished grade elevation and overhead line clearance dimensions; verify whether truck traffic is expected.

agentTrace.reasoning: Vertical clearance requirements cannot be verified without section views showing finished driveway grade elevation in relationship to overhead conductor sag. This is critical because conductor clearance is measured to the lowest point under load, requiring mid-span survey data.

applicableAreas: Vehicle parking and display areas on concrete pads beneath overhead electric lines
findings.comment: Site plan shows parking areas and driveways, and grading plan shows finished surface elevations, but no section views document vertical clearance from parking pad surface to overhead electric lines. Plans must include section views with dimension callouts showing clearance from parking pad elevation to lowest overhead conductor point (16 feet for parking without truck traffic, 18 feet with truck traffic, 12 feet minimum for residential pedestrian areas). applicableAreas: Any clearance dimensions shown on site plan sheets

Multi-conductor installations have conductors offset several feet from pole center. Currently, no clearance dimensions are shown on any plan sheets, so this measurement methodology cannot be verified. When clearance dimensions are provided, ensure dimension lines originate at the conductor location (not pole center) and extend to the outermost edge of the site feature being cleared.

agentTrace.reasoning: This requirement emphasizes that when dimensions are shown, they must originate at conductor (not pole), which is a common source of understated clearance violations. The instruction is provided to ensure correct documentation practice when clearances are eventually documented.

applicableAreas: All buildings, structures, and site features relative to overhead distribution electric lines shown on site boundary
findings.comment: UCM § 1.10.3 contains an absolute prohibition: customer facilities shall NOT be installed under or over Austin Energy overhead distribution facilities, distinct from the clearance distance requirements and independent of measured clearance. Existing survey shows OHE lines; site plan shows buildings and structures in proximity. Plans must affirmatively demonstrate that no buildings, building projections, overhangs, or other permanent structures are positioned directly beneath or above the overhead distribution conductor routing. Any facility within electric easement must maintain 7.5-foot clearance. Provide clearance verification on all plan sheets showing OHE routing relative to structures.

agentTrace.reasoning: The prohibition on structures under/over distribution lines is absolute and separate from clearance distance requirements. Plans must affirmatively confirm compliance with this prohibition. The proximity of buildings to OHE shown on plans requires explicit verification that no violations occur.

applicableAreas: All locations where overhead electric lines are adjacent to proposed buildings, driveways, parking, or other structures with vertical clearance concerns
findings.comment: Vertical clearances from overhead electric lines to buildings, driveways, and parking areas appear potentially marginal based on site elevations and estimated overhead line heights shown on existing survey. No registered surveyor mid-span clearance survey data is provided. When overhead lines cross or are adjacent to site features with height constraints (driveways requiring 16-18 feet, buildings requiring clearance), a registered professional surveyor must provide measured pole and conductor elevation data showing actual mid-span clearances. Hire registered surveyor to conduct mid-span clearance survey showing actual conductor elevations and clearances to all site features.

agentTrace.observation: Sheet 4 shows approximate topographic elevations and pole locations. Sheets 9 and 11 show building and driveway elevation data. However, no surveyed conductor elevation data or mid-span clearance measurements are provided. The existing survey note on Sheet 4, Block 9 states: 'THIS SURVEY WAS PERFORMED WITHOUT THE BENEFIT OF A CURRENT TITLE COMMITMENT AND THERE MAY BE EASEMENTS... NOT SHOWN OR NOTED HEREON' — indicating survey limitations.
agentTrace.reasoning: When vertical clearances are critical to project feasibility (driveways requiring 16-18 feet clear), mid-span conductor elevation data from registered surveyor is essential. Estimating clearances from pole location alone introduces risk of violation at mid-span sag point.

applicableAreas: Decorative outdoor lighting fixture locations near overhead electric lines

Site plan notes state decorative lighting must be full cut-off and fully shielded per Land Development Code, but clearance from overhead lines is not addressed. Provide dimension callouts on landscape plan showing clearance from light fixture locations to outside conductor, or provide relocation notes for fixtures within clearance zones.

agentTrace.reasoning: Decorative lighting fixtures positioned under overhead lines present hazard. Clearance must be verified through dimension callouts.

applicableAreas: Tree planting locations on landscape plan near overhead electric distribution and transmission conductors
findings.comment: Landscape plan (Sheet 31) shows trees in proximity to overhead electric line (OHE) running along southern and eastern boundaries, identified only by classification codes (M, SY, PL) without species identification. No lateral distances from trees to conductors are documented. Trees within 10 lateral feet of overhead distribution conductors (or 50 lateral feet of transmission conductors) must be from the Utility Compatible Shade Trees list (ECM Appendix F, species marked 'UC', generally mature height ≤20 feet). Provide tree species identification on landscape plan by reference to plant schedule (Sheet 32 or detailed plant list), verify species against ECM Appendix F utility-compatible list, and document lateral distances from trees to OHE. Relocate any non-compatible trees outside the clearance zones.

agentTrace.observation: Vision review of Sheet 31 identified tree symbols near OHE line with codes (M, SY, PL) but no species names. Sheet 32 (tree list) provides surveyed existing tree inventory but does not appear to include proposed landscape trees with species identification. Vision analysis confirmed no lateral distance measurements from proposed trees to OHE.
agentTrace.reasoning: Trees near electric lines require two-step verification: (1) species identification against utility-compatible list (ECM Appendix F), and (2) distance measurement from tree location to conductor. Both are missing from current plans. Additionally, voltage of OHE is not confirmed (10 ft for distribution vs. 50 ft for transmission), requiring conservative 50-foot standard.

applicableAreas: Down guy wire anchor locations shown on existing survey conflicting with proposed accessible paths, driveways, or other site features

Down guy wires and anchor locations must be verified against all proposed site features and either relocated or resolved through pole conversion. Provide down guy relocation notes or conversion specifications for any poles with down guys that conflict with site improvements.

Easement exhibit must show dedicated easement for transmission down guy anchors extending 10 feet either side of guy wire alignment plus minimum 50 feet beyond end of anchor point. agentTrace.reasoning: Transmission down guys require dedicated easements with specific dimensions (10 feet either side of guy wire plus 50-foot extension beyond anchor). These must be shown on easement exhibit.

applicableAreas: Down guy anchor points from distribution poles on site

agentTrace.reasoning: Down guy anchors require dedicated easements to prevent site disturbance of ground anchor points. Easements must be shown on plat/easement exhibit.

applicableAreas: Construction staging areas, equipment operation zones, and work platforms during site construction
findings.comment: During construction, staging areas, crane swing radii, material storage, scaffold locations, and equipment operation zones must maintain 10-foot radial clearance from energized overhead electric lines per OSHA 1910.333. This is a working clearance requirement distinct from permanent clearances. No construction phasing plan or logistics plan has been provided in the site plan package showing staging area boundaries and confirming 10-foot working clearance during all construction phases. Provide construction logistics plan or phasing plan showing staging areas and confirming 10-foot radial clearance from OHE during all construction phases.

agentTrace.reasoning: OSHA working clearance requirements apply during construction and differ from permanent clearances. Without a construction plan showing staging areas and equipment zones, compliance cannot be verified.

applicableAreas: Cover sheet or general notes for project with overhead electric lines and construction activities
findings.comment: Texas Health & Safety Code Chapter 752, Section 752.003 requires plans to include a note that owner/contractor must notify Austin Energy at least 48 hours before work begins near high-voltage overhead lines. This note is not present on the cover sheet or general notes sheets. Review of Sheets 1 and 3 found no such notification requirement. Add a general note on cover sheet stating: 'Owner/Contractor must notify Austin Energy at least 48 hours before commencement of any work near high-voltage overhead electric lines per Texas Health & Safety Code Chapter 752, Section 752.003.'

agentTrace.reasoning: This notification requirement is mandated by state law and must be explicitly stated on plans. Its absence represents non-compliance with statutory documentation requirement.

applicableAreas: Service-mast through-roof installations on proposed buildings

If service masts are proposed through roofs, building elevation sheets must document mast locations and roof clearance dimensions. If service masts are not used (all underground service), this requirement is not applicable. Clarify service installation method and provide elevation documentation if roof-mounted masts are proposed.

agentTrace.reasoning: This requirement is not-verifiable because the service installation method (roof-mounted vs. underground) is not clearly documented in provided plans, and no building elevation sheets are available to show mast locations relative to roofs if used.
